page: Microsoft Azure L160ias_v5 is an isolated, storage-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Lasv5 family, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system provides 160 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs driven by AMD processors. System memory capacity totals 1280.0 GB, which establishes a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server utilizes an isolated hardware configuration, ensuring single-tenant resource assignment at the physical host level. No graphical processing accelerators are present, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Storage architecture is defined by 30720 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity integrated into the host node. In addition to high-capacity local non-volatile media, the server supports Azure Premium Storage attachments for persistent managed disk configurations. The substantial local NVMe storage volume allows systems to sustain large-scale local read and write operations without relying on external network-attached storage volumes for operational working datasets.

In qualitative terms, the resource profile emphasizes high density across compute, memory, and physical disk capacity. Coupling over 30 TB of local NVMe storage with 1.28 TB of RAM enables consolidation of data infrastructure that would otherwise require multiple smaller nodes to aggregate equivalent volume. Tradeoffs include managing the localized failure domain intrinsic to direct-attached NVMe storage, as data durability requires application-level replication across nodes.

The L160ias_v5 is structured for enterprise workloads characterized by demanding disk throughput and large memory footprints. Primary operational fits include distributed NoSQL databases, large relational database engines, high-volume data warehousing, analytics pipelines, search indexing engines, and transactional batch processing.
